summary: Tested the subscription model end to end on the backend and frontend. Backend: wrote a new pytest suite, tests/test_subscriptions_v2.py, with 39 tests and all 39 pass. It covers the exact plan prices and limits, the 25 templates and their collections, export credits (401 when signed out, request_id validation, duplicate request_id not charged, 402 with upgrade:true after the limit), template locks for every plan, features_used gating, bg-removal authorization and counting, background locking, /me entitlements, Team-only brand, Razorpay checkout (pro yearly = 45000 paise, basic monthly = 1800), verify with a bad signature (400, plan not activated) and the webhook returning 503. Admin coverage: plan update, persistence and restore, POST /admin/plans returning 405, template access per plan, template create/publish/delete with a frame overlay and rejection of JPEG frames, subscription grant, date change, extend and cancel, report, metrics, payments, user detail, suspend/reactivate, audit entries, and 403 for non-admins. Frontend (Playwright with real Clerk sign-in for free, basic, pro, team and admin): editor credits pill, photo sliders and rotate-90, effects/bg-remove/bg-upload locking per plan with toasts, NEEDS X badges (19 locked for Free, 14 for Basic, 4 for Pro, 0 for Team), the signed-out dialog with the sign-in button, the upgrade dialog after credits run out, a Pro export using one credit with a bg-removal authorization call (200), Pricing month/year prices, the Razorpay checkout iframe opening, the dashboard plan/credits/reset/expiry and saved cards, Team branding save and share on mobile, and the admin Plans edit dialog, Templates new/publish/delete with frame upload, Subscriptions report and payments table, and the user Manage grant form. One real backend bug found: admin grants with a future start date stay 'pending' forever and never activate.

critical.issue: A grant whose start_at is in the future gets status 'pending', and no code ever moves it to 'active'. expire_sweep only expires subscriptions and ACTIVE_STATES = active/trialing/past_due, so the user never receives the plan. Reproduced: granted Pro with start=now+5s, waited 10s, /me still showed plan free and the sub was still pending. The same grant also cancels the user's current non-payment access straight away, so the user loses their plan until the future start date, and then gets nothing.

minor.issue: Extend always sets status 'active', even for a pending sub with a future start or a canceled sub. A pending grant becomes active early, and extending a revoked sub silently reactivates it.

When an admin disables a plan (active=false), every current subscriber, including paying ones, drops straight to Free because of the p.get('active') check. Disabling should probably only hide the plan from new purchases.

If Razorpay returns 'authorized' (auto-capture off), the payment stays authorized and the plan only activates through the webhook. The webhook secret is not configured yet, so such a payment never activates. Either call capture or make sure auto-capture is enabled on the Razorpay account.
Buying a different paid plan cancels the existing payment subscription immediately, with no proration or credit for the remaining time (for example a yearly Pro user buying Basic loses the Pro year).
The credit is taken before the in-browser MediaPipe step runs. If the model download or inference fails, the credit is lost unless the frontend retries with the same request_id.

design_issues.screen: Admin user Manage dialog / subscription Dates
issues: grant-start-input, grant-end-input and sub-start/end inputs use the browser's native <input type=date> picker instead of the shadcn Calendar/Popover, which looks different from the rest of the dark UI

action_items: Fix pending subscriptions: in expire_sweep (or active_subs), set status 'active' for subs with status 'pending' and start_at <= now. Also don't cancel the user's current non-payment access when the new grant starts in the future (cancel it at the new start date instead, or keep both).
admin_extend: keep the status 'pending' while start_at is in the future. Decide whether extending a canceled sub should be allowed.
Decide what disabling a plan means. Probably hide it from /plans and checkout while existing subscribers keep their entitlements.
Handle 'authorized' payments in /billing/verify (capture through the API) or document that auto-capture must be on, and configure RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
Optional: replace native date inputs in the admin grant/dates forms with the shadcn Calendar.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1315 lines; split it into routers (billing, admin_subscriptions, admin_catalog, me).

features_used is reported by the client, so a modified client can leave out advanced_effects/custom_backgrounds to avoid the 402. This is acceptable because effects are rendered in the browser, but treat it as advisory and don't rely on it for billing.

Templates with plans=[] are treated as available to every plan, including Free (can_use_template). The admin form lets an admin untick all plans, which silently makes a template free for everyone. Consider requiring at least one plan.
Rate limiting is in memory and per process, so it resets on restart and isn't shared between workers. The export limit of 40/min per IP can also affect users behind a shared NAT.

rca of the issue: Pending grants: admin_grant sets status='pending' when start > now (server.py line 941). The only status sweep is expire_sweep (line 148), which only changes active->expired. ACTIVE_STATES excludes 'pending', so active_subs never returns the sub. Repro: POST /api/admin/subscriptions with start_at a few seconds in the future, wait, then GET /api/me: plan_id stays 'free'. Fix: in expire_sweep add update_many({status:'pending', start_at:{$lte:t}}, {$set:{status:'active'}, $push:history}). Also, admin_grant's update_many cancels existing non-payment subs immediately; only do that when the new sub starts now.
